name: X-linked Corneal Dermoid

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Corneal Dermoid

criteria.description: Presence of congenital, well-demarcated, elevated corneal lesion with dermoid characteristics
Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern
Histopathological confirmation showing choristomatous tissue with epidermal and dermal elements
Exclusion of other ocular surface tumors or malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital corneal dermoid lesion with histopathological confirmation and family history consistent with X-linked inheritance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not routinely available.

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing elevated, well-circumscribed corneal lesion
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography showing lesion depth and corneal involvement
genetic: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes linked to X-linked corneal dermoid (if available)
other: Histopathology demonstrating choristomatous tissue with epidermal and dermal elements

distinguishingFeatures: Usually sporadic and not inherited in X-linked pattern
May be associated with Goldenhar syndrome
Often unilateral but can be bilateral
Broader spectrum of tissue types involved
May involve conjunctiva and sclera in addition to cornea

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth or change in appearance
Development of corneal ulceration or infection
Significant visual axis obstruction causing amblyopia
references: Klintworth GK. Corneal dermoids and epibulbar choristomas. Surv Ophthalmol. 1982;27(4):233-246.
Duke-Elder S. System of Ophthalmology, Vol. 7, Part 1: The Cornea. 1965.
